html:
Claudius Ptolemy was a Greek astronomer, geographer and mathematician who worked in Alexandria in Roman Egypt in the 100s CE, in the city of the old Library. His books ruled astronomy and mapmaking for some 1,400 years.

  • The Almagest put the Earth at the centre and moved the planets on circles riding on circles, epicycles. With its star catalogue of over a thousand stars, it predicted the sky well enough to stay in use from Rome to Baghdad to Renaissance Europe.
  • The Geography gave latitudes and longitudes for thousands of places, from Ireland to China. It names many peoples, such as the Galindai of the Baltic, heirs of the Western Masurian culture.

In Alexandria Hypatia and her father worked on his texts. Scholars of Baghdad's House of Wisdom translated him into Arabic, and later astronomers argued with him: Ibn al-Haytham wrote a book of doubts about his models, and the Maragheh observatory built better ones. Copernicus in 1543 put the Sun at the centre and began the end of his system. In China his near contemporary Zhang Heng was doing similar work.
